course.name: A2 Grammar: Everyday Accuracy with Nguyen Minh Ha

topicDescription: Describe an action in progress in the past and a shorter event that interrupted it.

lessons.title: Actions in Progress at a Past Time
lessons.objective: Form affirmative and negative past continuous sentences for actions in progress at a stated past time.
lessons.description: Use was or were with a verb ending in -ing to describe a past action in progress.
lessons.content: Use was/were + verb-ing for an action that was in progress at a particular past time. Use was with I, he, she, and it; use were with you, we, and they. Add not after was/were for a negative sentence.
examples: At nine last night, I was reading.
They were waiting outside at six.
Mina was not sleeping at that time.
commonErrors: Do not use did with a past continuous verb: I was studying, not I did studying.
Choose was/were to match the subject: we were, not we was.
lessons.guidedPractice: Underline the past time, identify the subject, then choose was/were + verb-ing.
lessons.summary: Past continuous uses was/were plus -ing for an action in progress at a past time.

questions.questionText: At eight last night, I ___ a book.
questions.explanation: I takes was, and reading describes an action in progress at eight.

questions.questionText: At this time yesterday, the children ___ in the garden.
questions.explanation: The plural subject children takes were; the action was in progress.

questions.questionText: At ten last night, Lan ___ television; she was doing her homework.
questions.explanation: Lan takes was, and the negative is was not/wasn't plus watching.

questions.questionText: We ___ for the bus at 7:30 yesterday morning.
questions.explanation: We takes were, and the time tells us the waiting was in progress then.

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes an action in progress at 5 p.m. yesterday?
questions.correctAnswer: He was cooking dinner at five.
questions.explanation: Was cooking describes an action in progress at a particular past time.

options.text: He was cooking dinner at five.
He is cooking dinner at five yesterday.
He did cooking dinner at five.
He were cooking dinner at five.

questions.questionText: At midnight, my parents ___; they were still awake.
questions.explanation: Parents takes were; the negative form is weren't sleeping.

questions.questionText: At 6:15 yesterday, the shop assistant ___ the front door.
questions.explanation: The singular subject takes was plus the -ing form opening.

questions.questionText: At that moment, you ___ to the guide.
questions.explanation: You takes were, including when it refers to one person.

questions.questionText: At 9 p.m., Hoa and I ___ our project in the library.
questions.explanation: Hoa and I means we, so use were finishing.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct negative sentence: They ___ at 11 p.m.; they were on the train.
questions.explanation: They takes were, and the sentence needs a negative past continuous form.

lessons.title: Past Continuous Questions with Was and Were
lessons.objective: Ask and answer yes/no and wh- questions about actions in progress at a past time.
lessons.description: Move was/were before the subject and use question words to ask about past scenes.
lessons.content: For a yes/no question, put was or were before the subject: Were they working? For a wh- question, put the question word first: What was she carrying? Keep the main verb in the -ing form.
examples: Were you waiting at the station?
What was Nam doing at six?
commonErrors: Do not add did to a was/were question: Was she cooking?
Keep -ing after was/were: What were they doing?
lessons.guidedPractice: Find the subject and auxiliary, then place was/were before the subject in questions.
lessons.summary: Past continuous questions begin with was/were, or a wh-word followed by was/were and the subject.

questions.questionText: ___ you studying at nine last night?
questions.explanation: A yes/no question with you begins with were.

questions.questionText: What ___ Mai doing when you called?
questions.explanation: Mai takes was; the main verb stays in the -ing form.

questions.questionText: ___ the workers repairing the road at 6 a.m.?
questions.explanation: The plural subject workers takes were at the start of a question.

questions.questionText: Why ___ your brother carrying an umbrella?
questions.explanation: Your brother is singular, so use was after why.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: Put were before they and keep the main verb in the -ing form.

questions.questionText: Where ___ you sitting during the meeting?
questions.explanation: You takes were in the past continuous question.

questions.questionText: ___ the baby crying when you entered the room?
questions.explanation: The singular subject baby takes was at the start of the question.

questions.questionText: What ___ the students discussing at lunchtime?
questions.explanation: The plural subject students takes were.

questions.questionText: Which question asks about an action in progress at a past time?
questions.correctAnswer: Was Linh talking to the doctor at two?
questions.explanation: Was plus subject plus talking asks about an action in progress at two.

options.text: Was Linh talking to the doctor at two?
Did Linh talked to the doctor at two?
Is Linh talking to the doctor at two yesterday?
Was Linh talk to the doctor at two?

questions.questionText: How ___ they travelling to the airport when you met them?
questions.explanation: They takes were in a past continuous wh- question.

lessons.title: Interrupted Events with When
lessons.objective: Combine a longer action in progress with a shorter completed event using when.
lessons.description: Use past continuous for the background action and past simple for the interrupting event.
lessons.content: Use past continuous for an action already in progress and past simple for a shorter event that interrupts it. When often introduces the shorter event: I was walking home when it started to rain. The order of the clauses can change without changing the meaning.
examples: She was cooking when the phone rang.
When the lights went out, we were watching a film.
They were crossing the road when the bus stopped.
commonErrors: Do not use past continuous for both actions when one short event interrupts another.
The verb after when can be past simple for the interrupting event.
lessons.guidedPractice: Mark the longer background action and the shorter event, then choose the tense for each.
lessons.summary: Use past continuous for the action in progress and past simple for the event that interrupts it.

questions.questionText: I ___ home when I ___ my old teacher.
questions.explanation: Walking was in progress; seeing the teacher was the shorter event.

questions.questionText: When the doorbell ___, Dad was taking a shower.
questions.explanation: The doorbell ringing is the shorter interrupting event, so use past simple.

questions.questionText: They were having dinner when the lights ___.
questions.explanation: The lights going out is the short event that interrupts dinner.

questions.questionText: When I ___ the room, the children were doing their homework.
questions.explanation: Entering is the shorter completed event; doing homework was already in progress.

questions.questionText: A taxi ___ while we were waiting in the rain.
questions.explanation: The taxi stopping is a completed event during the longer wait.

questions.questionText: My phone ___ while I was talking to the receptionist.
questions.explanation: The phone rang is the short event that happened during the conversation.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.correctAnswer: While we were walking, it began to snow.
questions.explanation: Walking was in progress; began is the completed event that interrupted it.

options.text: While we were walking, it began to snow.
While we walked, it was begin to snow.
While we were walk, it began to snow.
While we are walking, it began to snow.

questions.questionText: She ___ a photo when the guide asked everyone to move.
questions.explanation: Taking the photo was in progress when the guide asked them to move.

questions.questionText: The students were writing when the teacher ___ the classroom.
questions.explanation: The teacher entering is the shorter completed event.

questions.questionText: When the bus arrived, we ___ for it outside.
questions.explanation: Waiting was in progress when the bus arrived.

lessons.title: When and While in Short Narratives
lessons.objective: Choose when or while and combine past continuous with past simple in short narratives.
lessons.description: Use while to frame an action in progress and when to introduce a past event or time point.
lessons.content: While commonly introduces the longer action in progress: While I was studying, my friend called. When often introduces the shorter event: I was studying when my friend called. Past continuous can also describe two actions happening at the same time, but this lesson focuses on clear A2 narratives.
examples: While Mum was driving, I was reading the map.
I dropped my keys while I was opening the door.
We were talking when the manager arrived.
commonErrors: Use while with an action in progress when the context calls for a background action.
Do not change the short interrupting event to past continuous unless the meaning is also an action in progress.
lessons.guidedPractice: Read each two-event situation, identify the background and interrupting event, then connect them with when or while.
lessons.summary: When and while connect past events; use past continuous for the background action and past simple for a short completed event.

questions.questionText: ___ I was walking to the shop, I met my neighbour.
questions.explanation: While introduces the longer action that was in progress.

questions.questionText: We were watching the news ___ the electricity went off.
questions.explanation: When introduces the shorter event that interrupted watching.

questions.questionText: While the chef ___ dinner, a guest knocked on the door.
questions.explanation: The preparation was in progress, so use was preparing.

questions.questionText: I was carrying the boxes when one of them ___.
questions.explanation: The box falling is a short completed event; fall changes to fell.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence with the correct tense contrast.
questions.correctAnswer: While they were travelling, they stopped at a small village.
questions.explanation: Travelling is the background action; stopped is the completed event.

options.text: While they were travelling, they stopped at a small village.
While they travelled, they were stop at a small village.
While they were travel, they stopped at a small village.
While they are travelling, they stopped at a small village.

questions.questionText: The phone rang ___ we were having a meeting.
questions.explanation: While links the ringing event to the meeting that was in progress.

questions.questionText: What ___ you doing when the storm started?
questions.explanation: The question uses were with you before the -ing form doing.

questions.questionText: While I was looking for my passport, my sister ___ me from the airport.
questions.explanation: The call is the short completed event during the search.
questions.knowledgePoint: past simple interruption in a narrative

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes two events with the correct order and tenses?
questions.correctAnswer: I was washing the dishes when my brother arrived.
questions.explanation: Washing was already in progress; arrived is the shorter event.

options.text: I was washing the dishes when my brother arrived.
I washed the dishes when my brother was arrive.
I was wash the dishes when my brother arrived.
I am washing the dishes when my brother arrived.

questions.questionText: While the children were building a model, their father ___ them some glue.
questions.explanation: The father giving glue is a completed event during the ongoing activity; give changes to gave.
